page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.large is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8559C processor operating at 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, presenting two vCPUs across a single physical core with two threads. Advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX are supported, paired with a 320 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 16.0 GB of high-frequency 6 GHz DDR5 RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is a bundled 1,250 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity provides a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth. No hardware GPU acceleration is included.

Benchmark outcomes show sharp divergence between single-threaded and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core compute capability is strong, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2,289.0 in the top 10 percent of recorded instances, alongside single-threaded compression speeds of 34.71 GB/sec in gzip and 14.08 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. However, because the instance relies on only one physical core, parallel computing marks are constrained: multi-core stress-ng tests place in the bottom 10 percent, while Geekbench multi-core (2,800.0) and PassMark CPU metrics (4,125.74) place in the lowest quartile. Memory bandwidth across large uncached blocks tests around 22 to 23 GB/sec.

From an operational and efficiency perspective, i7ie.large balances a compact compute footprint with high local NVMe storage density and generous DDR5 memory. While aggregate parallel processing power is naturally limited by the dual-vCPU ceiling, the provision of over 1.2 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage without requiring external EBS volumes delivers strong qualitative I/O value. The server fits single-threaded data manipulation, mid-sized local caching nodes, lightweight database replicas, and log ingestion pipelines needing high local NVMe throughput with modest CPU demands.
description: Amazon Web Services i7ie.large is an x86_64 storage-optimized Nitro instance powered by a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8559C processor. It provides 2 vCPUs from a single physical core, complemented by 16.0 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory and a dedicated 1,250 GB local NVMe SSD, with baseline networking at 2 Gbps. The architecture delivers exceptional single-threaded performance, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 2,289.0 and fast data decompression rates. Due to its dual-thread single-core topology, parallel multi-core computational throughput is modest, as reflected in lower multi-core benchmark percentiles. However, the abundant local NVMe storage capacity paired with 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU offers a cost-effective platform for I/O-heavy applications that do not demand extensive core counts. It is well suited for log ingestion engines, intermediate data caching, and compact transaction databases.
